This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.
SCCH-5 2

. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 11.02.2022 at about 5.00 a.m. petitioner had been travelling from Bengaluru to Saundatti in VRL Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-63-5329, the driver of the said bus was driving at heavy speed in rash and negligent manner, when he reached near Hubli-Haveri National Highway, near Devagiri Village bridge of Haveri District, the driver of the bus lost control over vehicle and but tilted twice and fell down on the extreme left side of the bridge, as a result, petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to Government District Hospital, Haveri, thereafter shifted to Manipal Hospital, for which she has spent an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses.

3. At the time of the accident she was aged about 53 years, hale and healthy, serving in Police Department, SCCH-5 thereby drawing salary of Rs.30,058/- p.m. due to the accidental injuries, she is unable to do her day-to-day activities, she has also lost two months salary.
Out of this accident crime No.23/2022
is registered against the driver of the said VRL Bus before the Haveri Rural Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337, 338 and 304(a) of IPC.
Respondent No.1 is the insurer, respondent No.2 is owner of the said offending vehicle, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 18% p.a.
4.

On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has appeared and filed written statement and denied entire averments of the petition and further stated that, petition is barred by limitation as the alleged accident SCCH-5 took place on 12.02.2002 and petition came to be filed in December 2002.
It is submitted that, this tribunal has not territorial jurisdiction to entertain the petition.
Further denied age, occupation and income of the petitioner, injuries sustained, treatment taken and expenses incurred by the petitioner.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5. Respondent No.2/insurer has appeared and filed written statement and denied averments of the petition.

Further stated that, its liability to pay the compensation is subject to terms and conditions Lata.D vs Vrl Logistics Ltd on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57856867/
2 of the policy, existence of valid RC, FC, permit and driving license of driver of the offending vehicle.
He is entitled to take shelter under Sec. 170 of M.V.Act.
Further denied age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
Claim made SCCH-5 by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

6. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1. Whether Petitioner proves that, on 12.02.2022 at about 5.00 a.m. when the petitioner was travelling in the VRL Bus bearing Reg.No. KA-63-5329 Ashok Leyland,
near Hubli-Haveri National Highway, near Devagiri Village Bridge, Haveri District, at that time, driver of the said Bus was driving at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner due to which the bus fell down and tenant petitioner sustained grievous injuries, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?

If so from which respondent?
3. What order or award?
SCCH-5 7.
In order to prove his case, Petitioner herself deposed her evidence as PW-1 and marked 13 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.13 and closed her evidence.
On the other hand, there is no evidence of respondents.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
9. Issue No.1:- In order to prove her case, petitioner has deposed her evidence as PW-1, in her chief-examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in her petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence SCCH-5 affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of statement of Krishna Siddappa is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.5.

Lata.D vs Vrl Logistics Ltd on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57856867/
3 10.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1 and records those have marked i.e., as FIR, complaint, statement of witness, spot mahazar and charge sheet corroborates the case of the petitioner about causing of the accident dated 11.02.2022 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
11.

Per contra, except appearance, filing of written statement, respondents have not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no SCCH-5 hesitation to believe the case of the petitioner about causing of the injuries to the petitioner out of the accident held on 11.02.2022 at about 5.00 a.m. while she was travelling in VRK Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-63-5329 near Hubli-Haveri National Highway, near Devagiri Village Bridge, Haveri District.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
12. On the other hand, there is no defence evidence and the police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the driver of the VRL Bus.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioner, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioner has proved the above issue No.1 in her favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
SCCH-5 13. Issue No.2:-

As per the evidence of the petitioner, she had sustained burst fracture with normal neurology, multiple thoratic and lumbar vertebral body bone edema/undisplaced vertebral fracture,
maubrium fracture with multiple left sided rib fractures.

In this regard she has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.6, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.8 issued by Manipal Hospitals, wherein he took treatment as indoor patient since 13.02.2022 to 17.02.2022.
14.

As per the case of the petitioner, she was aged about 53 years, for proof of her age, the copy of aadhar card is on record, wherein it is clearly mentioned year of birth of the petitioner as 1969 and the alleged accident is occurred in the year 2022, accordingly relying on copy of aadhar card, her age is considered about 53 years as on the date of accident.
SCCH-5 15
. As per her case, petitioner was serving in Police Department, thereby drawing salary of Rs.30,058/- p.m.
To prove the said facts, she has not produced any documents, except police endorsement marked as Ex.P.10 towards availment of leave.
In cross- examination of PW-1 dated 20.04.20243, she has categorically admitted that, she is continuing her service in Police department.
Further she admitted that, she has received half months salary for the leave availed by her during treatment.
As per own admissions of the PW-1, she is continuing in her service and availed salary for the period when she has undergone for treatment.

Under such circumstances,
petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income on account of disability and loss of income during laid up SCCH-5 period.
Further petitioner has not examined the Doctor to support her case.

Lata.D vs Vrl Logistics Ltd on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57856867/
4 16.

Further admittedly she has exhibited copy of the medical bills amounting to Rs.79,905/- marked as Ex.P.9, medical bill of Rs.2,140/- marked as Ex.P.11, diagnostic report marked as Ex.P.12 and Manipal Hospital Estimate bill marked as Ex.P.13.

Further as per the admissions of PW-1 in her cross-examination, the medical bills those spend as per Ex.P.9 for a sum of Rs.79,905/-, Rs.58,256/-
has been reimbursed under Aarogya Bhagya scheme and for remaining amount only she is entitled.

She has also admitted that, even after causing of the accident, she has continued in service in Police department and on the said facts, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has also argued that, as per the admissions of the petitioner, she is not entitled for SCCH-5 future loss of income and petitioner is entitled for remaining medical bills of Rs.21,649/-, medical bills of Rs.2,140/- as per Ex.P.11, diagnostic report bill of Rs.3,800/- marked as Ex.P.12, so totally petitioner is entitled for Rs.27,589/- towards medical expenses.
17. Per contra, except denial in the written statement, respondents have not taken any endeavors to step into witness box nor to prove the allegations as alleged in the written statement.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence, merely respondents have filed written statement and they have denied entire case of the petitioner are all not sufficient to disbelieve the petitioner case, because it is bounden duty of them to prove the defence as taken in the written statement.
Further except cross-examining the PW-1 orally, they have not taken any steps to disprove the case of the petitioner.
SCCH-5 Accordingly petitioner is entitled for medical bills and other compensation as stated below.
18. Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-
Sl.No .
Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1. Pain and sufferings 20,000-00 2.
Conveyance, nourishment and 20,000-00 attendant charges 3. Loss of amenities in life 20,000-00 4.
Medical Expenses 27,589-00 Total 87,589-00 19.
Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.87,589/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

20. In the case on hand, respondent No.2 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing SCCH-5 No.2403003121P104120003 which is valid for the period from 02.08.2021 to 01.08.2022 in respect of VRL Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-63-5329, the alleged accident was occurred on 11.02.2022 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.
Hence naturally liability of R1 shall go against R2, so that, R2/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
Lata.D vs Vrl Logistics Ltd on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57856867/
5 21. Issue No.3:
For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:

::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
SCCH-5

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.87,589/- (Rupees Eighty Seven Thousand Five Hundred Eighty Nine Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioner is entitled to get release entire award amount through e-payment directly to her account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

(MANJUNATHA K.P.) VIII ADDL. JUDGE, COURT OF SMALL CAUSES & ACJM,
BENGALURU.
